newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower on South America ideas.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower on South America ideas.

text.p: Ongoing talk of nearly ideal crop weather in South America plus aggressive selling by Rosenthal Collins pressured CBOT soy product futures to a lower close, traders said.
Rosenthal Collins sold 800 lots of January soymeal and also sold 800 lots of March soyoil, traders said.

Early support in soymeal came from cold weather in the U.S. Midwest which is boosting livestock feed usage, traders said. Support to soymeal also came from strong stopping of the deliveries posted Friday against the expired December contract, the traders said.
Traders also said the recent active export pace of U.S. soymeal was supportive but volume was thin and trading was quiet as the market enters a holiday atmosphere.
Soyoil closed 0.05 to 0.23 cent per lb lower, with January down 0.23 at 23.09 cents. Soymeal was $0.10 to $2.20 per ton lower, with January down $0.10 at $230.00.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated at 19,000 contracts, about the same as the 19,025 traded Thursday, according to the CBOT.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 16,000 contracts, below the 20,946 traded Thursday.
